question.text: Which withdrawal strategy minimizes the risk of depleting the retirement corpus too quickly?

answer.text: Withdrawing a large lump sum at the start of retirement for major purchases
Following a systematic withdrawal plan (SWP) with annual review of withdrawal rates
Withdrawing all interest and dividends immediately as received
Making no withdrawals for the first 10 years to let the corpus grow

explanation.text: The Logic: A systematic withdrawal plan with periodic review aligns withdrawals to the corpus and its performance over time and helps manage the risk of early depletion. The Trap: Large early withdrawals (Option A) permanently lose the benefit of compounding. No withdrawals for 10 years (Option D) may not be practical for ongoing income needs. Note: The workbook supports SWP and planning periodic withdrawals, and separately recommends an annual review of the retirement plan to manage early-withdrawal risk.
